name: Faricimab
route_note: intravitreal injection monthly for loading, then every 8–16 weeks

discovery.note: A CrossMAb bispecific IgG1 with one arm against VEGF-A and one against angiopoietin-2, and an engineered Fc that does not bind FcRn or Fc-gamma receptors. Year is the priority date of the Roche bispecific anti-VEGF/anti-ANG-2 antibody patent (US 8,945,552).

tagline: First bispecific antibody for the eye, blocking VEGF-A and angiopoietin-2
summary: Faricimab is a bispecific antibody that neutralises both VEGF-A and angiopoietin-2. By targeting two pathways that destabilise retinal vessels, it allows injection intervals of up to 16 weeks in wet age-related macular degeneration, diabetic macular oedema and retinal vein occlusion.
mechanism: VEGF-A promotes neovascularisation and leakage, while angiopoietin-2 antagonises the stabilising Tie2 receptor signalling of angiopoietin-1, making vessels leaky and more responsive to VEGF.

Faricimab binds and neutralises both factors, reducing leakage and promoting vascular stability. Its Fc region is engineered to abolish FcRn binding, shortening systemic half-life and limiting systemic exposure.
uses: Macular oedema after retinal vein occlusion

history.title: Phase 3 results
history.detail: TENAYA/LUCERNE (wet AMD) and YOSEMITE/RHINE (DME) show non-inferior vision with extended intervals.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Vabysmo approved in January for wet AMD and diabetic macular oedema.

history.title: EU approval
history.detail: Authorised in the EU in September.

history.title: Retinal vein occlusion
history.detail: FDA approves use in macular oedema after retinal vein occlusion.

history.title: Prefilled syringe
history.detail: A prefilled syringe presentation is approved.

facts: Faricimab was the first bispecific antibody approved for injection into the eye.
After loading doses, the label allows intervals of up to 16 weeks between injections in wet AMD and DME.
It was developed under the code name RG7716.
